get.description:
Returns player overlap data between games. Each object in the response shows how much a game overlaps
with other games in terms of player base. Supports Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox platforms.

When paginating through all games, use `cursor` and `limit`. The `limit` defines how many unique games to retrieve. Since games may be released on multiple platforms, the number of returned items can be higher.
Note: `limit` must be set to 1 when no specific game is selected.

To get data for a specific game, use `vgiId`, `slug`, or `steamAppId`. The response will include one entry per platform the game is available on.
get.summary: Get all player overlap data of games.

get.description:
All-in-one endpoint that retrieves the historical data of games. The data is returned as an array of objects, each object representing the historical values of a game on the given day. This endpoint returns all dates for all games since their release date, but no earlier than 2014-01-01.

Use the date parameter to select the date by which the results are selected. The date must be in the format YYYY-MM-DD. The earliest date available is 2014-01-01.
You can use the `cursor` and `limit` parameters to paginate through the results. The `limit` parameter specifies how many games will be returned. Since each game may have data for multiple platforms, the number of returned entries may be higher than the specified limit. The limit parameter must be between 1 and 1000. The total number of results of the given day is returned in the X-Total-Count header. You can optionally use the steamAppIds parameter to retrieve the results of specific games on the given day.

Alternatively, if you select specific games (via VGI IDs, slugs, or Steam App IDs), you can get all historical data in one request.
get.summary: Get all historical data of games.

parameters.description: Date by which historical data is selected. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest value: 2014-01-01.
parameters.name: date
